sentences: Revolving credit utilization is by far the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises sharply once utilization reaches about 0.72 of the credit limit.
The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and having at least one delinquency raises default risk.
Income is also a moderate driver that lowers risk at higher levels, though it matters less than delinquencies.
Length of credit history has at most a weak to moderate effect, with longer histories associated with lower risk, though the data do not settle its exact size or shape.
Debt-to-income ratio, number of dependents, age, months at address and recent inquiries each have negligible effects on predicted default.
The effect of utilization is larger when the applicant has more past delinquencies.
The data do not settle whether utilization and credit history length interact in a way that matters.
Utilization and income do not interact in any practically meaningful way.
